name: Kaylee Egerer
detail: The Herald of 22 Feb 2011 captions her Campus Improvements Chair, a term the archive does not record. It has her in 2008-09 and 2011-12 only, so her portrait had to be filed to the latter.

name: Paige Settles
detail: Recorded twice in the same year, as Page Settles and Paige Settles, both Speaker of the Senate. One person, two spellings. Her own progression, freshman senator in 2012-13, confirms the Herald was right to call her a senior in September 2015 and wrong to call her a junior the following March.

name: Nolan Miles / Noland Miles
detail: Entered twice in the same year under two spellings, as Chair of Public Relations and Chair of Student Affairs. One man: he is Executive Vice President in 1914-15 and 1915-16 as Nolan. His portrait attaches to the Nolan spelling, so the Noland entry reads as a person with no face and inflates the missing count.

name: Spirit Masters booklets 2011-2018
detail: Called the best untapped portrait source by an earlier researcher. All seven were pulled and searched against the whole missing list. Seventeen name matches, and twelve were different people entirely: Steve Todd served 1969-70 and Scott Taylor 1975-76, neither can be in a 2014 booklet. Of the three whose service plausibly overlapped, not one bio mentions student government. The source is spent; do not mine it again.

name: Carlene and Darlene Lodmell
detail: Two people, not one, despite differing by a single letter. They held office side by side: in 1995-96 Darlene chaired Student Affairs while Carlene chaired Legislative Research, and in 1996-97 Carlene was Vice President while Darlene was Secretary. A name-similarity sweep flags them every time; they must not be merged and neither may wear the other's face. Confirmed independently against the university's own records on 1 September 2026. This is settled and is now recorded in CLAUDE.md.

name: Amanda Allen / Amanda B. Allen
detail: Recorded as Executive Vice President and as Administrative Vice President in the same year, from two different sources. Probably one person whose title one source got wrong, but the two offices are genuinely distinct and nothing settles it, so no portrait was shared between the records.

name: 1989 Talisman, printed pages 352-353
detail: One leaf is missing from the TopSCHOLAR scan of the 1989 Talisman. PDF leaf 178 ends on printed page 351 and leaf 179 opens on printed page 354, so the index runs A to Crawford and then jumps to Foe. The whole D and E section of the index, and the first half of F, is simply not in the file. That is why Bill Engle cannot be looked up in the volume that covers his first year. Every leaf after 178 is therefore one printed spread further on than the arithmetic suggests: pages are 2*leaf-6 up to leaf 178 and 2*leaf-4 after it.

name: TopSCHOLAR Talismans 1982-1991
detail: Every volume of this run is scanned at about 96 dpi, roughly 816 by 1123 pixels per printed page, except the 1983 volume which is 1892 by 2386 and has no OCR text layer at all. At that ceiling a class portrait cell comes out between 70 and 160 pixels wide, which is small but real, while a face in a club or Associated Student Government group photograph comes out at 40 to 60 pixels, which is not usable for anything. Plan on the class portrait grids and treat the group photographs as name lists, not as picture sources. Volume record numbers run 405 for 1982, 406 and 407 for the two parts of 1983, then 408 to 415 for 1984 through 1991. Leaf to printed page: 1982 page = leaf-3; 1983 part 2 page = leaf+193; 1984 and 1991 page = 2*leaf-6; 1985 page = 2*leaf-4; 1988 and 1990 page = leaf-3; 1989 see the entry above.

name: Debby Clark
detail: Two Deborah Clarks sit in the same block of the 1974 Talisman senior grid, and three researchers left her open rather than guess. The disambiguator is Chi Omega, not hometown. The Herald of 6 November 1973 calls the legislative intern an Associated Student Government and Chi Omega member; the 1974 index puts Chi Omega on p. 259 and indexes only Deborah Kelly Clark there, Janca appearing on 248, 311 and 350. The grid prints them as DEBORAH J. CLARK, Elem. Ed., Campbellsville and DEBORAH K. CLARK, Admin. Services, Bowling Green. Hers is the second face in the third row. Do not reopen without a source that puts a different Clark in the office.

There is no 1995 volume: record 419 and its neighbours are the Xposure magazines, which carry no portrait grids, so the 1994 Talisman is the last book with grids and the 1994-95 intake has to be caught in it a year younger. NAMED IN AN INDEX BUT ONLY ON ORGANIZATION OR STORY PAGES, so they never sat for a portrait: Karl Miller, "Miller, Karl 162, 165" in 1991, the Public Relations Students Society of America spread; Alan Thomason, "Thomason, Alan N. 222" in 1991 and "180, 226" in 1992, Sigma Phi Epsilon and the ASG group photograph; Ginger Markham, "Markham, Ginger 152, 202" in 1993, Alpha Delta Pi and Spirit Masters, and "229" in 1992; Susan Mitchell, "Mitchell, Susan 170, 204" in 1993, 204 being the ASG group photograph; Heather Renee Meenach, "Meenach, Heather 144, 188, 202" in 1993 and "218" in 1992. kind: leaf to printed page, per volume
name: Talismans 1991-1994 on TopSCHOLAR
detail: Checked against printed folios, not assumed, because the arithmetic differs per volume and the note left for 1982-1991 does not hold for these scans. Every leaf after the TopSCHOLAR cover sheet is a two-page spread. 1991 (record 415): left page = 2*leaf - 8, verified at leaf 184 = p. 360. 1992 (416): left page = 2*leaf - 8, verified at leaf 64 = pp. 120-121. 1993 (417): left page = 2*leaf - 2, verified at leaf 15 = pp. 28-29 and leaf 25 = pp. 48-49. 1994 (418): left page = 2*leaf - 6, verified at leaf 141 = p. 276. Native scan width is 1760 px per spread for 1991 and 1992, 1728 for 1993, and 816 px per single page for 1994, so a class portrait cell comes out 90 to 160 px and a face in a club group photograph 35 to 50 px. The 1994 file has no OCR text layer of any kind, only the cover sheet.

name: Nicki Seay / Nicki Taylor
detail: A researcher found the Herald of 26 August 2014 captioning the ribbon cutting at the Downing Student Union with 'Student Government Association President Nicki Seay', while the archive records the 2014-15 president as Nicki Taylor and has no Seay in that year. It looked like a missing presidency, which is the most serious thing this archive can get wrong, and it is not one. They are one woman: CLAUDE.md already settles Janet 'Nicki' Seay and Nicki Taylor as a name change, and name-aliases.json maps them. The Herald used her earlier name a few months after the change. Both years carry a portrait. Nothing to do.

name: Elizabeth White / Lizzy White
detail: Almost certainly one person entered twice. The 2005 election special calls her a Nashville sophomore in her second semester in SGA, which puts her first semester in autumn 2004. The researcher filed the same mugshot under both rows deliberately so the duplication stays visible, and flagged it rather than merging.

name: Austin Wingate
detail: An earlier researcher left open whether the 2012 presidential candidate was the 2008-09 senator. He is: the story of 20 March 2012 says he served three years in SGA, two as senator and one as speaker, before standing down for a year, which places his first year at 2008-09. No usable photograph of him exists; the 2012 story is text only and every other frame is a group with no positions given.

name: WKU's own SGA executive headshot directories
detail: The live server still serves these files; only the directory listing is blocked, so a 403 does not mean the images are gone. Three archived directories exist, wku.edu/sga/<YYYY-YYYY>-executive/headshots/, for 2018-19, 2022-23 and 2023-24, named firstname_lastname_min.jpg. They gave up Lyndsey Kelley, Annalise Finch and Sydney Denney at 4480 by 6720, better than anything else for their years. The current executive page uses a different scheme: wku.edu/sga/2025_2026_executive/headshots_website/ with underscores in the year and short forms for filenames, caden.jpg and gabipace2.jpg, so it cannot be guessed and must be read off wku.edu/sga/executive/index.php, where each portrait sits beside the person's name and office. All five current executives already have faces. Every naming pattern was tried against the four executives still missing from 2018-19 and 2022-23 and none resolved, so the route is spent apart from watching the live executive page as each new year is published.

name: WKU Spirit Masters class booklets 2012-2017
detail: dlsc_ua_records 8497 (2012) through 8502 (2017), one booklet per class, each about 22 pages of studio portrait plus biography. All six were downloaded and all six carry a clean OCR text layer of 22,000 to 30,000 characters in which the members' names read correctly. Not one of the 72 executive officers still without a portrait is named in any of them. The 2011 booklet (8496) had already been worked. This closes the Spirit Masters route for the executive cohort; it may still be worth searching for senators.

name: wku.edu SGA executive headshot directories
detail: Probed every /sga/<year>-<year>-executive/ and /sga/<year>_<year>_executive/ path from 2011-12 to 2024-25 on the live server on 1 September 2026. Only four still exist, and a directory that exists answers 403 while one that never existed answers 404: 2018-2019-executive, 2022-2023-executive, 2023-2024-executive and 2024_2025_executive. Only 2023-2024-executive has a headshots/ subdirectory, and that one has already been mined; its files are served at 200 even though the listing 403s, with names of the form firstname_lastname_min.jpg. Nothing under 2018-2019 or 2022-2023 is reachable by any guessed filename or subdirectory (headshots, headshots_website, images, photos, pics tried). The current officer page at /sga/executive/index.php serves the 2025-2026 headshots from /sga/2025_2026_executive/headshots_website/, a third naming scheme. web.archive.org refused every connection through this pass, so the older directories were not testable there.

name: SGA's own election candidate booklet, spring 2013
detail: wku.edu/sga/debate/s13candidates.pdf is SGA's own two-page Spring 2013 Election candidate booklet: every candidate for president, executive vice president and administrative vice president gets a name heading, a photograph directly beneath it and a full biography. It placed Cain Alvey and Brad Cockrel. It is the only file left in /sga/debate/, and s12, s14, s15 and f13 equivalents all 404, so this appears to be the sole surviving year. Worth remembering as a document type: SGA published candidate booklets with portraits, and other years may survive elsewhere on wku.edu or in the Wayback Machine.

detail: Read at the exact alphabetical position from the page images with Apple Vision OCR, because the embedded 96 dpi text layers mangle surnames and a miss in them proves nothing. DREW DELOZIER: absent from the 1987 index; in 1988 the one entry is 'DeLozier, Drew 38', the ASG election story on pp.38-39, where he is named twice in the body and not photographed; he cannot be checked in 1989 because that scan is missing the leaf carrying the whole D and E index. SHANNON MONTGOMERY: 1990 gives 'Montgomery, Shannon - 162', which is the Associated Student Government group photograph, where she is fifth in the middle row of fourteen at about 20 px a face; absent from the 1991 index (it runs Monroe, Moody, Moon) and from 1992, 1993 and 1994. The 1994 volume is the last with portrait grids, and its People section is by residence hall rather than by class, so anyone living off campus is not in it at all.

name: Spirit Masters booklets 2012-2017
detail: dlsc_ua_records 8497 to 8502, all six downloaded and all carrying clean OCR text where member names read correctly. Not one of the seventy-two executives still without a face appears in any of them. This was billed as the best portrait lead for those years and it is closed. The Spirit Masters SCRAPBOOKS in stu_org are a different collection and are not covered by this.

name: SGA's own election candidate booklet
detail: wku.edu/sga/debate/s13candidates.pdf gives a name heading, a studio photograph and a full biography for each candidate, which is the best identification this archive accepts. It placed Cain Alvey and Brad Cockrel outright. It is the only file left in /sga/debate/: s12, s14, s15 and f13 all 404, and the elections page links no booklets at all. If another year of this document type surfaces anywhere it is worth a run on its own.

note: Record pages on digitalcommons.wku.edu serve 200 to a plain script. The file endpoint /cgi/viewcontent.cgi does NOT: it still returns 403 to curl while the human's own browser gets 200 on the same URL, because the block is on the TLS fingerprint and no header or cookie reproduces it. An agent reported the block lifted after seeing a record page succeed; it had not. Reading catalogue metadata is fine from a script. Downloading a scanned volume is not, and scripts/browser_bridge.py exists for that.

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE INTO TOPSCHOLAR, found 4 September 2026
note: TopSCHOLAR's file endpoint /cgi/viewcontent.cgi refuses every script and even headless Chrome with a 403; the block is on the TLS fingerprint. The Internet Archive has mirrored those same PDFs and serves them to plain curl. Fetching http://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=<N>&context=dlsc_ua_records returned a real 4.6 MB Herald issue on the first try. Get <N> from the record page, which curl CAN read with -L: it carries the viewcontent link. The `id_` in the wayback path matters, it asks for the raw file rather than the archive's HTML wrapper. The PDFs carry an OCR text layer but it is close to unreadable on these scans; render at 300 dpi with PyMuPDF and run ocrmac over the pages instead, which reads them well. This opens every scanned Herald and Talisman on TopSCHOLAR to plain scripts and removes the reason _topscholar-wanted.json existed.

topic: THE WAYBACK ROUTE, SECOND URL FORM
note: The cgi form web/2024id_/.../cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=N&context=C works for most of TopSCHOLAR but the Internet Archive has no snapshot of some items: context=stu_org articles 1342-1379 404 on it. A second form reaches those: web/2024id_/https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/context/<collection>/article/<N>/type/native/viewcontent That is how the Phi Mu composites came in, at 3400x2500. Try the cgi form first and fall back to this one; between them TopSCHOLAR is effectively open to plain scripts.

Every digitised Herald issue for 1997-2005, 537 of them and roughly 10,000 pages, has been OCR'd with ocrmac and the page text saved one JSON file per issue. It is kept at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_herald-ocr-1997-2005/, 133 MB, named <date>-a<article>.json. Search that before fetching anything: it is the difference between one grep and re-downloading ten thousand pages. It was built in /tmp and would have been lost at the next reboot.
